source.title: Generalizability of Memorization Neural Networks
source.authors: Li-Jia Yu; Xiao-Shan Gao; Li-Jun Zhang; Yibo Miao

page_placements.theme: Training fit does not determine generalization or representation quality

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices and experimental tables.
record.tranche_reason: The paper gives theoretical results and experiments on memorization networks’ generalization, but does not test the listed random-label, unstructured-input, noisy-label, regularization, or learning-order claims.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own results concern constructed memorization algorithms and their generalization on i.i.d. data. These do not test the listed claim versions. Its experiments compare true-label classification performance; those results also do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes explicitly constructed interpolating networks and their generalization under distribution and sample-size assumptions. Its experiments use true-label binary classification. Neither the constructions nor the SGD comparator test any of V1–V6; polynomial-time construction is not evidence about SGD convergence time.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: some constructed memorization networks generalize poorly despite large i.i.d. datasets, while an efficient construction guarantees generalization under stated distribution and sample-size conditions. The authors also establish structural and sample-complexity constraints and acknowledge that their algorithm trails SGD on CIFAR-10.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies theoretical memorization-network construction and generalization, plus experiments on true-label classification; it does not reproduce random-label SGD experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Theoretical generalization results depend on distribution assumptions and network structure or parameter count; the CIFAR-10 results vary by class pair.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 5.3 constructs an interpolating network with population accuracy at most 0.51 for any distribution satisfying its separation and density assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Perfect interpolation of i.i.d. training data can coexist with poor population accuracy in explicitly constructed networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 7.3 provides a polynomial-time interpolation algorithm with a generalization guarantee above a distribution-dependent sample threshold. Its true-label CIFAR-10 accuracies are 0.54–0.87, versus 0.96–0.99 for the trained ResNet18 comparator.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Constructed interpolation algorithms can have conditional generalization guarantees while performing worse empirically than SGD-trained networks.

record.peer_reviewed: 38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024)
record.problems: Theoretical guarantees require distribution assumptions. The paper says its algorithm cannot surpass normal training empirically on CIFAR-10. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported experiment tables.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 1 and 4 report additional true-label MNIST memorization-network accuracies, while Tables 2 and 3 report each CIFAR-10 label pair separately. These results do not test any listed version; only the CIFAR-10 memorization-versus-trained-comparator comparison is retained as an example of the experiments’ scope.

untested.parts: SGD fitting completely random labels with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, including training error and chance test performance.
Relative training time for true and random labels, and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and progressive test degradation across random-label corruption fractions.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels, including comparisons over training.

record.verdict_notes: Capacity to interpolate through explicit construction does not establish random-label fitting by standard SGD training. The paper's references to the original studies provide context, not additional tests of their claims.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks trained with stochastic gradient methods fit completely random labels with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and whether test error is at chance.
Training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Training and test performance across levels of random label corruption.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation on fitting random labels and generalization on true labels.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.

rows.subject: memorization network F for Dtr
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 5.3 constructs a memorization network for an i.i.d. dataset and bounds its accuracy on D.
rows.note: The result is a theoretical construction for a distribution with density r; it does not concern random labels or SGD.
rows.check: The stated accuracy bound and parameter count match Theorem 5.3, but this is an existential construction deliberately arranged to generalize poorly, not a random-label SGD result. Its original observed state cannot describe any listed version.

rows.subject: memorization network L(Dtr)
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 7.3 gives an efficient memorization algorithm and a generalization guarantee.
rows.measure: Probability that population accuracy is at least 1 − ε
rows.note: This is a theoretical result for the paper’s constructed algorithm, not standard SGD training.
rows.check: The guarantee matches Theorem 7.3, but concerns a constructed algorithm on distributions with positive separation between opposite labels. It measures none of the listed effects; observed is inapplicable.

source_check.problem: Accurate theoretical guarantee; the constructed algorithm and separated-label distributions do not test V1–V6.

rows.subject: memorization algorithm by Theorem 7.3
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated on CIFAR-10 binary classification tasks using 3,000 samples per class; the table reports test accuracy by class pair.
rows.value: Table 2 reports pair-specific accuracies from 0.54 to 0.87; the authors state most are above 70%, with cat and dog among the poor results.
rows.note: True-label classification experiment; values are reported separately for label pairs and do not test a listed claim version.
rows.check: The 0.54–0.87 test-accuracy range is correct. This summarizes the study's own method's performance on true labels and should not be a claim-evidence row. It also aggregates multiple class-pair conditions.

source_check.problem: Accurate range across class pairs, but the study's own method performance should be contextual information rather than claim evidence.

rows.subject: Resnet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the same CIFAR-10 binary tasks for 20 epochs, learning rate 0.1, with crossentropy loss.
rows.value: Table 3 reports pair-specific accuracies from 0.96 to 0.99; the authors say the training results are significantly better than Table 2.
rows.note: True-label comparator, not a random-label or memorization test as specified by the versions.
rows.check: The 0.96–0.99 test-accuracy range and training settings match the text. This is a true-label comparator for the study's method and should not be a claim-evidence row; no random-label or regularization contrast is reported.

relation.reason: Discusses memorization and generalization without testing random-label SGD fitting or the other listed claim versions.

tranche.reason: Constructive interpolation and generalization theory, with true-label classification experiments, neither tests nor uses the specific effects in V1–V6.
